headline: Learned molecular predictors tested under cold-start and cross-species transfer
label: Evaluating Learned Molecular Predictors
summary: Recent work pairs learned predictors with explicit split and cold-start tests that probe generalization beyond in-distribution fit.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of learned predictors under conditions that probe transfer rather than in-distribution fit. The biorxiv toxicity study curates a 50,603-record aquatic dataset, releases the tox-learn library, benchmarks splitting strategies, and introduces 3DMol-Tox for cross-chemical and cross-species prediction. The DAVIS curation provides 4,032 modification-aware kinase-ligand pairs and three benchmark settings for testing generalization. MMDDI reports cold-start accuracy alongside hit@4 of 0.86, and the published active learning framework reports 13- to 17-fold hit-rate gains in prioritizing compounds. What is new is the pairing of model design with explicit split and cold-start evaluation. This thread does not extend to every item: HyperADRs, Rep3Net, RoBep, CrossPPI, MotiL, and ENGINE primarily present architectures or pretraining objectives for prediction.
